L8·N1516unmasked layer
Fires on a concrete noun/modifier that opens a multi-word compound term or list item, typically right after a determiner, possessive, or "and" (e.g. "particle" in "particle physics laboratory", "driving" in "driving license", "Face" in "Face Invaders", "suppliers" in "employees and suppliers"); the analogous position with different nouns ("camp director", "green fluorescent protein") drives it negative, so it looks like a surface/positional noun-slot detector rather than a semantic category.

L8·N10730unmasked layer
This neuron fires at clause junctures — on the pivot token immediately after a completed clause or subject (auxiliaries like "will/is", a clause-closing comma or ")", the conjunction "and", or the first verb of a new sentence) — rather than on any content-word meaning; the same surface forms ("is", ",", "was") also produce the strongest negative activations, so it looks like a positional/syntactic-boundary feature with mixed sign.

L8·N12141unmasked layer
This neuron sits at the token right after a noun phrase and signals "noun-phrase continues": it fires on prepositions/modifiers extending the phrase (" in", " for", " Terminal", "regation") in catalog/promotional listing text, and is strongly negative on finite/copular verbs (" is", " was", " give") that instead turn the preceding noun into a clause subject.
